editorial.description_en: Green taken as far down as it goes while still being green. Reads black indoors and green outside, which is the whole reason it is in the corpus.
editorial.description_ja: 黒に近いところまで暗くした緑。
editorial.contemporaryNote_en: The green counterpart to 深宵 in the Indigo group: a substitute for black that keeps a hue. Its behaviour under changing light is the argument for it and also the risk in it.

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.258, C 0.048, h 146.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 黒 (kuro, black) + 緑 (midori, green). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Black Green" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 黒緑. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — fuyu-sugi at ΔE00 6.5, iwa-hada at ΔE00 7.7, shin-en at ΔE00 9.4. complementary is empty because no entry in this corpus sits within 22° of the opposite hue. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
